## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use the `codex://threads/` URL format. When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days. ## OpenCode GitHub Actions To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user. Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation. The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward. When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. // Start gameplay once without guessing between multiple controls or following links.
export async function startForCapture(page, { enabled = true, selector = '', timeout = 3000 } = {}) {
  if (!enabled) return { clicked: false, reason: 'disabled' }
  const candidate = selector
    ? page.locator(selector)
    : page.locator('button, input[type="button"], input[type="submit"], [role="button"]')
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeout
  do {
    const matches = []
    for (const control of await candidate.all()) {
      if (!await control.isVisible() || !await control.isEnabled()) continue
      const eligible = await control.evaluate((element, explicit) => {
        if (element.closest('a[href], form') || element.getAttribute('aria-disabled') === 'true') return false
        if (explicit) return true
        const label = element.getAttribute('aria-label') || element.value || element.textContent || ''
        return /^(?:start|play)(?:\s+(?:game|now))?$/i.test(label.trim())
      }, Boolean(selector))
      if (eligible) matches.push(control)
    }
    if (matches.length > 1) return { clicked: false, reason: 'ambiguous' }
    if (matches.length === 1) {
      try { await matches[0].click({ trial: true, timeout: 2000 }) }

  if (car.onGround) {
    // steer
    const steerAuthority = clamp(Math.abs(speedAlong)/7,0,1) * (0.35 + 0.65*...)
    car.yaw += input.steer * 2.7 * dt * clamp(Math.abs(speedAlong)/5, 0.15, 1) * (speedAlong < -0.5 ? -1 : 1)
    // throttle
    let accel = 0
    if (input.throttle > 0.01) {
      if (speedAlong < -1) accel = 30 * input.throttle // brake
      else accel = 19 * input.throttle
    } else if (input.throttle < -0.01) {
      if (speedAlong > 1) accel = 34 * input.throttle // brake harder
      else accel = 13 * input.throttle // reverse
    }
    if (car.boost meter>0 && input.boost) { accel += 24; ...}
    car.vel.x += forward.x * accel * dt...
    // grip lateral
    const latx = car.vel.x - forward.x*speedAlong, latz...
    const grip = input.boost ? 3.2 : 6.5 (lower while drifting maybe handbrake none)
    decay lateral: factor = Math.exp(-grip*dt)
    // drag

    // max speed
    const maxF = input.boost && boost>0 ? 38 : 23
    if speedAlong > maxF -> reduce along forward
    if speedAlong < -12 -> clamp
    // yaw rotates velocity with grip -> handled by lateral damping? actual velocity direction aligns because forward rotates and lateral gets damped.
  } else {
    // air control yaw, pitch not needed

    // slight air acceleration from throttle

  }
  // boost drain when input.boost and boost>0 (also in air)
  ...
  // jump
  if (input.jumpPressed) { ... }
  // vertical
  car.pos.y += car.vel.y*dt; car.vel.y -= gravity*dt
  if pos.y <= 0 { if falling hard -> bob; pos.y=0; vel.y=0; onGround=true; jumpCount=0; flipTime=0 }

## Objective
- Build a polished 3D browser game: 1v1 Rocket League-style car soccer versus a bot, first to 3 goals, in the current OMG PlayGround repo.

## Requirements
- "3D 1v1 Rocket League vs a bot, first to 3 goals"
- Game must work as a static site served by the runtime default server on port 3002.
- Mobile/touch support, responsive layout, and automated/browser verification expected by the project workflow.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js r170 vendored locally under `vendor/` with an import map, avoiding npm/Vite and network dependencies at runtime.
- Source files renamed from `.mjs` to `.js` because the runtime server serves `.mjs` as `application/octet-stream`; `src/package.json` (`{"type":"module"}`) keeps Node tests treating `src/*.js` as ESM.
- Custom arcade physics and AI are plain data/math in `src/physics.js` and `src/ai.js`, unit-testable in Node.
- Menu button intentionally labeled exactly `Play` with `aria-label="Play"` for the capture auto-start heuristic.
- Match flow: menu → 3-second kickoff countdown → play → goal celebration (~2.65s) → kickoff, ending with victory/defeat overlay at 3 goals.
- Default difficulty Pro, alternatives Rookie and All-Star; ball cam defaults ON; boost starts at 34 per kickoff, pads refill boost.
- Debug API exposed as `window.__rocket` with `startMatch`, `skipCountdown`, `forceGoal`, `endMatch`, `setScore`, `setBall`, `setCar`, `giveBoost`, `snapshot`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full game implemented: arena, goals/nets, stands/crowd, boost pads, car models, ball with hex texture, lighting/shadows, particles, synthesized audio, chase/ball/goal/result cameras, screen shake, HUD, minimap, pause menu, result screen, difficulty selector, keyboard/gamepad/touch input.
- Physics/AI unit tests: 10 passing via `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`.
- Verified in Chromium at 1440x900 and iPhone 15 emulation: menu, countdown, driving/boost, car-ball hits, real goal detection into net, bot scoring, goal banner, victory screen, pause overlay, touch joystick movement.
- Fixed mobile HUD overlaps by repositioning speedo, boost ring, pause, CAM button, toast, and rotate hint; mobile touch control hints added.
- Changed loading overlay to `pointer-events: none` to avoid blocking capture auto-start.
- `capture.sh` ran twice: mobile auto-start works; desktop still reports `auto-start not-actionable`.

### Active
- Investigating why `startForCapture` fails on the 1440x900 desktop capture despite `#playBtn` being visible, hit-testing as `playBtn`, and `locator.click({trial:true, timeout:4000})` succeeding in a separate direct Playwright script.
- Reproduced with runtime `startForCapture`: `{ clicked: false, reason: 'not-actionable' }` even though before-call diagnostics show loading removed, phase `menu`, button rect `{x:72,y:599.875,width:540,height:66}`, and scrollTop `0`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Debug `startForCapture` desktop failure: compare its candidate loop/trial-click behavior against the successful direct `#playBtn.click({trial:true})`; log which element/candidate causes the trial timeout.
2. Likely fix options: add `CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR=#playBtn` to capture invocation/workflow, adjust Play button CSS/animation stability (e.g., hover/`::after` shimmer), or make the button match actionability before capture runs.
3. Re-run `CAPTURE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3002 CAPTURE_DIR=/tmp/rocket-capture ./capture.sh` and confirm both `final-desktop.png` and `final-mobile.png` show live gameplay, not the menu.
4. Re-run `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` after any edits.
5. Optionally improve menu-side stats panel visibility/contrast and finish README project documentation.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game orchestration, UI, input, camera, effects, debug API.
- `src/physics.js`: arena constants, car/ball physics, collisions, goal detection, boost pads.
- `src/ai.js`: bot controller, difficulty presets, prediction/attack/defense logic.
- `src/world.js`: Three.js arena, cars, ball, lights, crowd, pads, shockwaves.
- `src/particles.js`: pooled additive particle system.
- `src/audio.js`: synthesized WebAudio effects/engine/crowd.
- `index.html`: DOM, HUD, menu, overlays, touch controls, import map.
- `styles.css`: all responsive/mobile styling.
- `tests/game.test.mjs`: 10 physics/AI unit tests.
- `src/package.json`: `{"type":"module"}` for Node tests.
- `vendor/three.module.js`, `vendor/addons/geometries/RoundedBoxGeometry.js`: local Three.js.
- `capture.sh`: runs runtime default capture; currently desktop auto-start issue.
- `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/capture-start.mjs`: auto-start heuristic causing `not-actionable`.
- `/tmp/rocket-shots/` and `/tmp/rocket-capture2/`: verification screenshots.
- `/tmp/click-test2.mjs`: reproduction script for `startForCapture` failure.

## Important Context
- Server running in tmux session `rocket`: `cd /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround && PORT=3002 node $RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs > /tmp/rocket-server.log 2>&1`.
- Playwright CLI sessions in use: default desktop, `-s=mobile`, `-s=cap`; display is Xvfb `:0`.
- Runtime Playwright was initially missing chromium build `1243`; installed via `playwright-cli install-browser chromium`.
- Renderer is SwiftShader/llvmpipe (`lowPower: true`), so frame rate/timing can lag; physics uses fixed 1/120 steps and countdown uses raw dt.
- Desktop capture failure evidence: `startForCapture` returns `not-actionable`; direct Playwright trial click succeeds and starts `countdown`.
- `window.__rocket.snapshot()` exposes phase, score, positions, stats, touch state, renderer, `lowPower`, triangles.
- Working tree changes are uncommitted; no commit/push has been made.

function simplifyMaterials(scene) {
  const cache = new Map()
  scene.traverse(obj => {
    if (!obj.material) return
    const list = Array.isArray(obj.material) ? obj.material : [obj.material]
    const next = list.map(m => {
      if (!m.isMeshStandardMaterial && !m.isMeshPhysicalMaterial) return m
      if (cache.has(m.uuid)) return cache.get(m.uuid)
      const simple = new THREE.MeshLambertMaterial({
        color: m.color, map: m.map, emissive: m.emissive, emissiveIntensity: m.emissiveIntensity,
        transparent: m.transparent, opacity: m.opacity, side: m.side,
        vertexColors: m.vertexColors, fog: m.fog, alphaTest: m.alphaTest,
        depthWrite: m.depthWrite, blending: m.blending, toneMapped: m.toneMapped,
      })
      cache.set(m.uuid, simple)

    })
    obj.material = Array.isArray(obj.material) ? next : next[0]
  })
}
